newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: NatGrid to report on Malaysian utility in a month.
newsitem.headline: NatGrid to report on Malaysian utility in a month.

text.p: U.K. consultant firm National Grid Group Plc will complete a report on Malaysia's Tenaga Nasional Bhd's operations in one month, the Business Times newspaper reported on Saturday.
Malaysia appointed National Grid earlier this week to examine the state-controlled utility's operations following a massive blackout in peninsula Malaysia on Aug. 3.

"We have just begun work on the study, which will take one month to complete," the newspaper quoted National Grid as saying. National Grid said it will be looking at five areas including the failure of a circuit breaker which Tenaga said triggered the chain of events leading to the blackout.

The consultants will also examine the performance of protection systems, the under-frequency load shedding and spinning reserve arrangements, the system recovery process and generation, the article said.
National Grid indicated that the focus of its study will be on improving the existing transmission and distribution system, the daily reported.
This is the second time National Grid has been called in to investigate Tenaga's operations. Malaysia also appointed the firm to check on the utility after a big power outage in 1992.
